purpose: Behavioral regression scenarios for complete delivery, layered reading, design file responsibilities, glossary increments, and agent decision boundaries
run_instructions: Give the executor SKILL.md, the reference files required for the current delivery format, and each scenario's context and request. Withhold expect.
Run each scenario independently. Simulate only the response and plan content; do not change the scenario's product, execute deletions, or publish issues.

Use expect to assess delivery scope, navigation, file responsibilities, question thresholds, and authorization boundaries. Inspect the simulated content of each file; keyword matches do not replace semantic judgment.
Rerun after changing the skill. Ordinary planning does not require reading these scenarios.

cases.title: A large feature must not shrink into a first version
cases.context: An existing monolithic Web application already has account permissions, background jobs, and a database. These are verified facts. There are no additional business ambiguities.
cases.request: Write an implementation plan for large-file uploads, resumable chunked uploads, progress display, cancellation, failure retries, history, and account isolation. You may divide the work into phases, but I want complete delivery. Give the plan only in chat; do not implement it.

expect.action: Deliver the plan directly without clarification questions
checks: Every requirement maps to work and acceptance
All phases lead to overall acceptance
The remaining full implementation is planned beyond the first phase
Prototypes or placeholders do not replace real functionality
The user is not required to invoke other skills or configure an issue tracker

cases.title: The agent handles known function behavior
cases.context: Verified facts: the project CSV parser skips blank rows and converts empty cells to null. The existing interface reports validation errors by row number. Imports with the same external ID use idempotent updates. Parser and permission regression tests exist.
cases.request: Write a plan for adding CSV customer imports, reusing the existing behavior. I need uploads, error preview, import confirmation, and result statistics. Do not implement it; respond only in chat.

expect.action: Deliver the plan directly without clarification questions
checks: Do not ask about empty strings, blank rows, duplicate IDs, or internal return types
Correctly reuse the verified semantics
Cover implementation and acceptance for upload, preview, confirmation, and statistics
Retain user-visible boundaries and permission regressions
Do not override the known idempotency convention

cases.title: A small complete plan is possible without repository access
cases.context: The target project code is inaccessible. The user has not requested a particular framework, and there is no issue tracker.
cases.request: Give me a development plan for a local batch-renaming tool: read a directory, preview names using a prefix and sequence number, detect name collisions, execute after confirmation, and support undo. Local offline use is sufficient. Give the plan only in chat.

expect.action: Deliver the plan directly without clarification questions
checks: Fully cover reading, naming, preview, collision detection, confirmed execution, and undo
Label technical selections as choices rather than existing project facts
Do not claim to have inspected code or verified commands without evidence
Choose a safe default that does not overwrite files
Do not add servers, cloud platforms, or an account system
Do not require tracker setup or details for every function

cases.title: An irreversible requirements conflict needs escalation
cases.context: Existing materials establish no priority, applicable exception, or retention policy.
cases.request: Write an implementation plan for customer deletion. Hard requirement one: clicking delete permanently removes all original customer content and every copy. Hard requirement two: all original content for the same customer must remain unchanged for auditing for ten years. Both are mandatory. Planning only.

expect.action: Identify the hard-requirement conflict, ask a material clarification question, and deliver a conditional plan for unaffected work
checks: Do not discard either hard requirement without authorization
Do not claim that anonymization, soft deletion, or retaining a copy satisfies both requirements
Provide a recommended tradeoff and its consequences for the user to confirm
Mark unresolved tasks as conditional without claiming the entire plan is unconditionally executable
Do not ask about unrelated function details

cases.title: Respect an explicitly limited prototype scope
cases.context: The user explicitly wants to validate a UI layout, not ship a product.
cases.request: Write only a plan for a single-page upload UI prototype using fake data. No backend, persistence, or production rollout. This is for comparing layouts. Deliver in chat.

expect.action: Deliver a prototype plan directly within the explicitly limited scope
checks: Do not use complete delivery as a reason to add a backend, database, or production deployment
Cover the single page, fake data, and layout comparison
Do not describe the prototype as a complete production product
Do not start an additional interview or implementation

cases.title: Repair a reduced plan by restoring work, not changing wording
cases.context: The original user requirements are uploads, progress, cancellation, failure retries, history, and account isolation. The existing plan says: the first version includes only uploads and simulated progress; cancellation and failure retries come later; history and isolation are out of scope. The user never authorized these exclusions.
cases.request: Revise this plan so it fully covers my original requirements. Give the revised plan only in chat.

expect.action: Revise the plan directly without repeating confirmation questions
checks: Restore work and acceptance for all six original requirements
Simulated progress cannot replace real task progress
Cancellation, failure retries, history, and isolation all have real implementation paths
Overall completion criteria cover every requirement
Merely removing phrases such as first version is insufficient

cases.title: Skipping a critical question is not approval
cases.context: The previous turn asked whether a migration may permanently delete audit records. The user skipped the question. Retention policy is unknown, and deletion is irreversible. The rest of the old and new read-interface migration and regression validation has sufficient evidence and can be planned now.
cases.request: Give me the migration plan first. Do not ask me to answer the previous question again. Planning only; do not execute.

expect.action: Avoid repeating the question and deliver a conditional plan that clearly marks the unresolved critical decision
checks: Do not treat skipping the question as permission for permanent deletion
Affected deletion or cutover work has an explicit decision gate
Unaffected tasks remain fully planned
Do not claim unconditional executability or approval to delete
Do not omit risks to make the plan appear complete

cases.title: Ordinary planning needs no skill chain and does not authorize implementation
cases.context: The existing project stores plans under docs/plans and has no issue tracker. An existing messaging service provides send and query interfaces. Frontend and backend test entry points are known.
cases.request: Write a plan for in-app notifications: sending, unread counts, marking as read, and history, reusing the existing messaging service. Do not change product code. In this response, describe what you would deliver and simulate the document content without actually writing files.

expect.action: Deliver the content of a complete plan and its location under the existing convention without clarification questions
checks: Cover all four requirements and overall acceptance
Complete the approach, work breakdown, and acceptance in one invocation; file count does not define a single entry point
Do not require grill, to-spec, to-tickets, issue tracker setup, or a session switch
Do not require user approval at every step
Do not install dependencies, change product code, create issues, or claim simulated documents were actually saved

cases.title: A complex plan separates design topics while retaining the complete roadmap
cases.context: Project conventions use docs/plans. The existing Web UI, upload service, database, and background-job entry points have been verified. Permission and regression tests can be reused. Requirements and technical choices have no material ambiguity.
cases.request: Plan large-file uploads, including resumable chunks, progress, cancellation, retries, history, and account isolation. Make the plan readable by responsibility and cover complete delivery. Simulate the default directory and the main content of each file in your response; do not write files or implement anything.

expect.action: Directly simulate the directory plan and file content without clarification questions
checks: The default directory is docs/plans/<topic>/, with README.md as the complete roadmap entry point
Shared design is split under the plan's ./design/, with design/README.md and no design.md containing every detail
Files such as architecture, flows, contracts, data, and ui contain only their relevant design, without mechanically generating all optional files
The design index states reading order, the question each file answers, and reasons omitted topics do not apply
Work-package files list required design links, requirement identifiers, dependencies, and local acceptance
The overview, tasks, and acceptance.md cover every requirement and overall acceptance; splitting loses no cancellation, retry, or isolation work
Do not duplicate design content, generate empty directories, or claim simulated files were actually saved

cases.title: A small task stays readable without empty directory scaffolding
cases.context: The only work is changing an existing button's disabled condition and adding one regression case runnable through an existing entry point. There are no new interfaces, terms, data, or cross-module designs. Existing materials and behavior are clear.
cases.request: Write the complete implementation plan using the default organization. Simulate its content and save location in your response without actually writing files.

expect.action: Deliver a small single-file plan directly without clarification questions
checks: The plan may use docs/plans/<topic>.md, keeping the goal, local approach, work packages, and acceptance together
Do not generate empty design, glossary, UI, or decisions files to satisfy a directory convention
Cover the disabled condition and regression verification without expanding into an architecture overhaul
Do not require issue tracker setup or another skill, or claim the simulated document was saved

cases.title: An explicit single-file request overrides the complex-plan default
cases.context: Requirements for large-file uploads with a UI, interfaces, background jobs, and persistence are clear. Normal, failure, and permission behavior all have supporting evidence.
cases.request: Write only one planning.md; do not create other files. Organize the complete plan with a table of contents and sections. Simulate the content in your response first without actually saving or implementing anything.

expect.action: Simulate one complete planning.md with sections and anchors
checks: Deliver only the requested single file without adding design/ or tasks/ files
Use a table of contents, clear sections, and traceable requirement and task identifiers to retain design, glossary increments, tasks, and overall acceptance
Complexity is not a reason to remove requirements or stop at the first phase
Do not claim simulated content was saved or change the product or project-wide documents

cases.title: The glossary records only increments and explicitly marks semantic changes
cases.context: The project glossary already defines "upload session" and "complete"; complete originally means the server has received all chunks. The user explicitly requires complete to mean validation has passed and adds "chunk receipt." Another term, "external confirmation," is unclear but affects only optional hint text and does not block the main approach.
cases.request: Write a directory plan for a cross-service upload flow, clearly explaining new terms and changes to existing ones. Simulate the main design-file content in your response without changing the glossary, ADRs, or product, or saving files.

expect.action: Simulate glossary increments in the design directory and link them to the approach and implementation tasks
checks: design/glossary.md records the new chunk receipt term and the semantic change to complete
The stable upload session term references its existing definition instead of creating a second glossary
The complete entry references the old definition and explains the evidence and scope of the new meaning
New or changed entries include definitions, relationships, evidence, status, and the implementation merge destination and work package
External confirmation retains an awaiting-confirmation status and its effects; do not invent a definition or make it an unnecessary blocking interview
Other files link to glossary entries; protocol and field details belong in contracts or data
Do not directly change the existing project glossary or global ADRs, or equate planning records with authorized implementation

cases.title: Generate optional designs by responsibility rather than filling a template
cases.context: A scheduled backend service needs batch queries, failure retries, and cursor storage across several independently assignable work packages. There is no user interface and no new or changed domain terminology. Existing architecture decisions remain valid, and the database and internal API have been verified.
cases.request: Organize an assignable directory plan. List the files you would generate and their content in your response without actually writing files.

expect.action: Provide a directory plan containing only relevant design topics
checks: Organize relevant interfaces, flows, and data under design/ rather than putting all details in one design.md
Explain the absence of UI, glossary increments, or new material decisions in design/README.md, reusing existing document links
Do not create ui.md, glossary.md, or similar files containing only a heading or none
Flows own retry behavior, contracts own inputs, outputs, and error semantics, and data owns cursor structure and persistence
Work packages link required designs and local acceptance; acceptance.md covers integration and regressions

cases.title: A long single-file migration preserves one authoritative entry point and valid references
cases.context: The existing docs/plans/upload.md is long and includes R1 chunked uploads, R2 cancellation, and R3 resume. WP-A and WP-B are referenced by other documents, and cancellation/resume integration is unfinished. A seven-day or thirty-day retention period still awaits the user's decision. External links point to the original plan entry point.
cases.request: Reorganize this plan into an overview, design/, and tasks/. Do not change the requirements or decide the retention period for me. Simulate the migration approach and file content in your response first without actually moving, deleting, or writing files.

expect.action: Simulate the structural migration while preserving identifiers, unresolved conditions, and valid references
checks: Original requirements and WP-A and WP-B remain traceable; unfinished integration appears in work packages and overall acceptance
Retain navigation at the original entry point or update known incoming links; do not leave two conflicting authoritative full plans
Move relevant design details into the corresponding ./design/ files; tasks live under tasks/ with direct required-design links
Keep retention unresolved and identify affected tasks; migration is not user authorization to decide it
Do not drop requirements, decision evidence, or still-referenced sections during migration, or claim the simulated migration actually occurred
